title: M30 Take-Profit 1 Expansion Test (10 to 15 Pips)
research_question: Does widening TP1 from 10.0 to 15.0 pips on the M30 timeframe increase the average win size and profit factor without lowering the win rate below the 75% threshold on GBPUSD?
hypothesis: Because M30 candle range is wider than M15, widening TP1 from 10 to 15 pips allows the initial partial close to capture a larger portion of the Fibonacci impulse move, boosting the profit factor on both training and 2025 validation partitions.

facts: EXP-0018 on M30 achieved Profit Factor 3.44 with an 81.25% win rate in training.
EXP-0019 on M30 achieved +$163.34 net profit with a 78.16% win rate in 2025 validation.
In EXP-0019, 68 winning trades averaged $20.64, while 19 losses averaged -$65.29.
inferences: Increasing TP1 from 10 to 15 pips on M30 will increase the average win payoff, strengthening the margin of profitability over losses.
On M30, a 15-pip target is well within the 1-2 bar impulse range.
evidence: EXP-0018 total_trades=16, profit_factor=3.44, win_rate=81.25%, total_net_profit=531.64, equity_drawdown_maximal_percent=2.35
EXP-0019 total_trades=87, profit_factor=1.13, win_rate=78.16%, total_net_profit=163.34, equity_drawdown_maximal_percent=3.88

independent_variables.name: InpTP1Pips
independent_variables.rationale: Widen first take-profit target to capture larger gains on M30 candles before partial close.

assumptions: Widening TP1 from 10 to 15 pips will not cause excessive trades to reverse before hitting TP1.
expected_observations: Total net profit on GBPUSD M30 exceeds baseline EXP-0018 ($531.64).
Average profit trade increases above $20.64 on 2025 validation.
falsification_conditions: Profit factor declines below baseline EXP-0018 (3.44) or EXP-0019 (1.13).
